newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey asks Israel to rethink new settlement.
newsitem.headline: Turkey asks Israel to rethink new settlement.

text.p: Turkey asked Israel on Friday to rethink a Jewish settlement project on occupied Arab land that has sparked international criticism.
"We hope that Israel will revise its policy regarding Har Homa and other (Jewish) settlements," the foreign ministry said in a statement.
Israel approved on Wednesday the building of thousands of new Jewish homes in Arab East Jerusalem, defying warnings the project could unleash a wave of Palestinian violence.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu defended the decision as an effort by his country to alleviate a shortage of housing for Arabs and Jews in the city. Palestinians see it as an attempt to cement Israeli's hold over all of Jerusalem.

Ankara said it was concerned the housing plan would hinder the Midde East peace process and it recalled the negative impact of the opening of an archaeological tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem last year.

Ties between Moslem but secular Turkey and Israel have grown since the signing of two military accords which involve allowing Israeli jets to go on training flights in Turkish airspace and the upgrading of the Turkish Air Force's fleet of F-4 Phantom jets by Israel.
Turkey's armed forces chief General Ismail Hakki Karadayi visited Israel this week in a further sign of strengthening military cooperation between the two countries.
